# The model

A document is one whole restoration of the seventeen lost verses: its $N$
content lemmata, however many there are, drawn from the mixture
$\sum_k \theta_k \phi_k$ with $\theta \sim \mathrm{Dirichlet}(\mathbf 1)$.
The topic-word distributions $\phi$ ($K \times V$) are **soft**: a lemma has
probability under several topics, so every word is a mixture and the posterior
$p(\theta \mid \text{document})$ has no closed form. $\phi$ is fitted once on
Aeschylus and Euripides by a seeded latent Dirichlet allocation (tomotopy),
so that Sophocles, the baseline, is a test corpus like the restorations and
$\phi$ is not fitted on the text it is then compared with; each
of the unsupervised clusters of the analytic model seeding one topic with
a strong word prior on all its lemmata, plus a few free topics.

The cells are those of the analytic model: the walk, one document per
untilted snapshot; Henry's seventeen verses, one document; and Sophocles'
extant trimeters in windows of seventeen, the reference. Every
cell is read on two levels: its **mean profile**, the documents' posteriors
averaged draw by draw, compared with Sophocles' by
$P(\bar\theta_k^{\text{cell}} > \bar\theta_k^{\text{Soph}})$ and the lift of
the means, and a **random document** against a random window,
$P(\theta_k^{\text{doc}} > \theta_k^{\text{window}})$. A topic is raised when
the mean-profile probability is at least 0.9 and the lift at least 1.5.

**Amortization.** A word enters the likelihood only through its $K$
log-likelihoods $\log \phi_{\cdot w}$, so a document is a set of $K$-vectors
and a DeepSet summary network is the natural compression. Documents differ
in length, so the set is padded and the network pools over the real elements
only, with $\log N$ as an extra summary. A coupling flow (BayesFlow) learns
$\theta$ in additive log-ratio coordinates from 200,000 simulated documents
whose lengths are drawn from the real documents' lengths. Before it reads
the real documents it is checked on 1000 held-out simulations: recovery
$R^2$, 90 % interval coverage, and simulation-based calibration (SBC), whose
rank histograms must be uniform if the posterior is calibrated.

The GPU work is done by `scripts/amortized_mixed_model.py`
(`slurm/amortized_mixed_model.slurm`); this document reads its output.

```{r load}
phi <- fromJSON(file.path(results_dir, "phi.json"))
result <- fromJSON(file.path(results_dir, "cells.json"))
cells <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "cells.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8")
sbc <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "sbc.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8")
recovery <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "recovery.csv"),
                     encoding = "UTF-8")

topic_names <- phi$names
K <- length(topic_names)                          # seeded + free topics
H <- length(result$cells$sophocles$p_dominant_seeded)   # seeded topics only
cell_names <- c("walk", "henry")
cells <- filter(cells, cell %in% c("sophocles", cell_names))
cells$cell <- factor(cells$cell, levels = c("sophocles", cell_names))

cat(H, "seeded topics and", K - H, "free topics;",
    "vocabulary of", phi$vocab_size, "lemmata;",
    "LDA log-likelihood per word", round(phi$ll_per_word, 3), "\n")
```

# The topics

The ten top lemmata of every topic as the seeded LDA fitted them on
Aeschylus and Euripides, with the number of seed lemmata found in the
vocabulary.

```{r topics, results = "asis"}
for (k in seq_len(K)) {
  topic <- topic_names[k]
  top_words <- paste(head(phi$top_words[[topic]], 10), collapse = " ")
  if (k <= H) {
    n_seeds <- length(phi$seeds_found[[topic]])
    cat("- **", topic, "** (", n_seeds, " seeds): ", top_words, "\n",
        sep = "")
  } else {
    cat("- **", topic, "** (free): ", top_words, "\n", sep = "")
  }
}
```

# Calibration of the amortized posterior

```{r checks}
checks <- data.frame(topic = topic_names,
                     recovery_r2 = result$checks$recovery_r2,
                     coverage90 = result$checks$coverage90,
                     sbc_p = result$checks$sbc_p)
knitr::kable(checks, digits = 2)
```

```{r sbc, fig.height = 6}
shown <- head(topic_names, params$show_topics)
sbc_shown <- filter(sbc, topic %in% shown)
sbc_shown$topic <- factor(sbc_shown$topic, levels = shown)
ggplot(sbc_shown, aes(x = rank)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "grey60") +
  facet_wrap(~ topic, ncol = 4) +
  labs(title = "SBC rank histograms (uniform if calibrated)",
       x = "rank of the true theta among the posterior draws", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(8)
```

```{r recovery, fig.height = 6}
recovery_shown <- filter(recovery, topic %in% shown)
recovery_shown$topic <- factor(recovery_shown$topic, levels = shown)
ggplot(recovery_shown, aes(x = true, y = post_mean)) +
  geom_abline(colour = "grey50") +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), colour = "grey80") +
  geom_point(size = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ topic, ncol = 4) +
  labs(title = "Recovery on held-out simulations (mean and 90 % interval)",
       x = "true theta", y = "posterior") +
  theme_minimal(8)
```

```{r sizes}
sizes <- unique(cells[, c("cell", "n_docs", "n_lemmata")])
knitr::kable(sizes, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "The cells: documents and content lemmata each")
```

# Topics raised above Sophocles

Seeded topics whose mean profile is above Sophocles' with $P \ge 0.9$ and a
lift of at least 1.5, with the lift, the posterior mean and, in brackets,
the document-level probability.

```{r raised, results = "asis"}
cells$raised <- !is.na(cells$lift) & cells$p_above_sophocles >= 0.9 &
  cells$lift >= 1.5
raised <- arrange(filter(cells, raised), cell, desc(lift))
for (cell_name in cell_names) {
  cell_raised <- filter(raised, cell == cell_name)
  if (nrow(cell_raised) == 0) {
    cat("- **", cell_name, "**: none\n", sep = "")
    next
  }
  items <- sprintf("%s (%.1f×, %.2f [%.2f])", cell_raised$topic,
                   cell_raised$lift, cell_raised$mean, cell_raised$p_document)
  cat("- **", cell_name, "** (", cell_raised$n_docs[1], " documents): ",
      paste(items, collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
}
```

# Lift of every seeded topic in every cell

```{r lifts, fig.height = 7}
lifts <- filter(cells, cell != "sophocles")
lifts$topic <- factor(lifts$topic, levels = rev(topic_names[1:H]))
ggplot(lifts, aes(x = topic, y = lift, fill = raised)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~ cell, ncol = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey70", "firebrick"),
                    name = "raised: P >= 0.9\nand lift >= 1.5") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "lift of the mean profile against Sophocles") +
  theme_minimal(8) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Which seeded topic dominates

```{r dominant, fig.height = 7}
heat <- cells
heat$topic <- factor(heat$topic, levels = rev(topic_names[1:H]))
ggplot(heat, aes(x = cell, y = topic, fill = p_dominant)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "firebrick",
                      name = "P(largest\nseeded topic)") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       title = "Which seeded topic dominates a random document of the cell") +
  theme_minimal(8)
```

The five largest mean profiles in every cell.

```{r mass}
top_five <- NULL
for (cell_name in c("sophocles", cell_names)) {
  cell_rows <- arrange(filter(cells, cell == cell_name), desc(mean))
  top_five <- rbind(top_five, head(cell_rows, 5))
}
top_five <- top_five[, c("cell", "topic", "mean", "q05", "q95", "lift",
                         "p_above_sophocles", "p_document")]
knitr::kable(top_five, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```
